title: A free common frequency law does not remove the tail-fit conflict in two selected CHIME bursts
abstract: We test a common exponential scattering tail in FRB20220428C and FRB20220428B, two CHIME bursts 2.04 seconds apart. The tail time and its frequency exponent are shared between bursts. We allow one or two intrinsic Gaussian pulses per burst and test two data compressions. In the main two-pulse fit, a free common exponent improves chi-square by only 0.27 over exponent -4. Separate free tail laws improve chi-square by 47.63 over the shared free law. This extends an earlier shared-tail test at fixed exponent. These are conditional model-fit results, not calibrated probabilities for a change in plasma. Intrinsic pulse shape, parameter limits, correlated noise and selection of this pair limit the physical claim. No independent telescope observation confirms the pair. Code, aggregate fit evidence, data hashes and separate-scratch reproduction steps are included. External intensity data are excluded.
